learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to basically operate the FE program ANSYS Workbench.

Students are able to independently create their own simple structural mechanical models to perform structural mechanical simulations, including: Definition of material properties, Geometry creation, Mesh creation, Definition of boundary conditions.
Students are able to generate their own structural mechanical simulation results, and to select, present and discuss the relevant results for the respective task.
Students are able to work on a project task together in a team (communication, discussion, finding consensus).
Students are able to complete a project task within a given timeframe and acquire and apply knowledge of project planning and management in the engineering field.
Students are able to combine their knowledge and connections from various sub-disciplines to solve complex tasks.
Students are able to present the result of the independent, scientific processing of the project task using the required standards and technical language.

syllabus_topics: Preprocessing, model creation, loads and boundary conditions
Solution (calculation run) and postprocessing (evaluation of stresses and deformations)
Thermal analyses and combined thermal-mechanical analyses
Material properties (linear elastic and elastoplastic input)

assessment_methods.method: Exercises and tasks for all program parts
Independent execution of a small strength analysis (project) using Finite Elements

assessment_rules: The course is graded, and the assessment components contribute 100% to the module grade.
